crossRefs.note: The king of Israel said to Elisha, when he saw them, “My father, shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?”
Now Elisha became sick with the illness of which he died; and Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over…
So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save…
Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Therefore let the young men find favor in your eyes; for we come on a good…
But I was willing to do nothing without your consent, that your goodness would not be as of necessity, but of free will.

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.line: King of Aram, besieged Samaria, contemporary of Elisha.

people.name: Damascus
people.line: Ancient city, capital of Syria, important in biblical history.

people.name: Hazael
people.line: King of Aram (Syria), anointed by Elijah.

people.name: Syria
people.line: Ancient region north of Israel, often in conflict

translations.web: So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, “Your son Benhadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’ ”
translations.bsb: So Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him a gift of forty camel loads of every good thing from Damascus. And he went in and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
translations.kjv: So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels' burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Benhadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
